title: 量化原生元数据作为因果可得的粗代理：Q1分块尺度 × 离线权重Gram预测FFN组效用

proposer.session_ref: 2026-10-24 user correction: quantization stored information should provide low-cost rough proxies, explicitly distinguish native FP4 from HiF4 QDQ

origin.note: Proposal returns to the user's earlier intent: quantizer-native cheap side information as an imperfect Q1-side ranking proxy, NOT exact code equality, memoization, or a replacement for W1 numerical outputs. Standard quantization-scale statistics, weight norms and routing are prior ingredients; the causal/physical combination and predictive viability are untested.

mechanism.native_flow: Original source-pinned Wan (D=5120,H=13824) computes modulation + Q1 → W1 + bias → tanh-GELU → Q2 → W2 → current gate + residual. In native reference tools/packed_ffn_reference.py, Q1/Q2 is HiF4 QDQ followed by BF16 F.linear; Q2 is followed by optional per-token gain alpha and BF16 cast before W2. Quantizer-created scale metadata for Q1 is available BEFORE W1 only if the actual operator materializes/exposes it; for Q2 it arrives AFTER W1, making it a potential W2/next-stage signal, not a free pre-W1 signal.
mechanism.information_object: Let x_t^Q=Q1(x_t) and divide its K axis into B blocks I_b of length 32 (MXFP4) or 16 (NVFP4). A native code/scale representation may satisfy x_{t,I_b}^Q=s_{t,b}^{eff}c_{t,b}, with c an E2M1 code vector; MXFP4 s_eff is an E8M0 shared 2^e value; NVFP4 s_eff is E4M3 16-wide local scale times effective FP32 global scale (recipe-dependent, including static versus dynamic and row scaling). HiF4 runtime uses a separate hierarchical 64/8/4 QDQ with BF16 activations, and does NOT currently promise persistent accessible scale bytes. Offline weight scales, norms, codebook occupancy and group matrices can be precomputed outside token inference.
mechanism.causal_proxy: For target W1 hidden group g, let A_{g,b}=W1[g,I_b] be the frozen effective W1 weights after the actual format-specific weight path. Write z_{t,g}-bias_g=Σ_b s_{t,b}^{eff} A_{g,b}c_{t,b}. Build nonnegative offline matrix K_{g,b}=ν_b ||A_{g,b}||_F² for a calibrated, source-separated code second-moment ν_b or a fixed calibrated prior. Online coarse proxy P_scale(t,g)=Σ_b K_{g,b}(s_{t,b}^{eff})². Under conditional zero-mean, block-independent isotropic code E[c_b c_bᵀ | scales]=ν_b I, this equals E[||z_{t,g}-bias_g||₂² | scales]. These statistical premises are NOT exact for correlated code, per-token modulation, GELU or bias. The score ranks potential preactivation energy, not GELU output, quality sensitivity or true net-value. Other targets can be learned/calibrated separately, with strong fixed-score and cheaper scalar baselines.
mechanism.low_cost_variant: Because g is 64-channel contiguous HiF4 hidden groups or another native Q2-compatible packing unit and b is an INPUT Q1 microscale block, they are DIFFERENT axes. For the 64-channel grouping example G=216, MX Q1 B=160 and NV Q1 B=320. Direct score matrix work per token G*B is 34560 / 69120 multiply-adds respectively versus D*H=70,778,880 MAC for W1 (arithmetic counts only, NOT elapsed-time ratios). A low-rank nonnegative or general factorization K≈UVᵀ of rank r changes the estimate to P≈U(Vᵀ s²), O(r(B+G)) arithmetic, e.g. r=8 gives 3008 (MX) or 4288 (NV) scalar ops per token plus reads/decision overhead; rank truncation and numerical distortion must be tested. Static global s² cancels only within-token homogeneous group ranking; it must not be canceled for cross-token thresholds or bias/GELU-dependent decisions.

quantizer_feature_ladder.feature: metadata-only: effective local scales, exponent-bin occupancy, log-scale spread, dynamic ratio to global scale, saturation/scale transition markers
quantizer_feature_ladder.availability: Before W1 only after Q1; score scale-amplitude + weight energy, no packed data scan beyond scale metadata

quantizer_feature_ladder.feature: tiny code samples or packed nibble summary: sign balance, second moment, nonzero fraction, low-bit plane, block code entropy
quantizer_feature_ladder.availability: Requires touching Q1 codes (possibly already in adjacent quantizing kernel; read/scan is not free). Can remedy scale-only ambiguity and signed direction to some extent

quantizer_feature_ladder.feature: offline low-rank W1 projection of sampled/pool codes and upstream AdaLN/gate/pre-norm residual cues
quantizer_feature_ladder.availability: More specific but strictly charge read/projection/memory/batching; avoid reconstructing hidden z in full
Only after W1; may inform W2 group decisions or temporal/next-stage cache; NEVER retroactively credit as W1 skip

mechanism.candidate_operator: The earliest candidate physical action is fixed-layout coarse W1 hidden-group selection or a small set of prepacked native Q2-aligned patterns. At equal budget, compare fixed selected groups (including random/frequency/weight-only), simple input norm or scalar scale, T0 weighted scale-Gram proxy, T1 code-enhanced version and a purpose-trained small router. Omitted groups are truly excluded from W1 and the corresponding W2 panels; no mandatory dense fill-in, rank256 recovery or dense oracle. For approximate paths the full-span uncomputed Q2 quantizer coupling / scale recalibration must be modeled; packing entire native scale groups avoids silently breaking backend semantics. No fixed 50% sparsity goal is presumed.
mechanism.decision_utility: Score usefulness is conditional on retained real FFN calculation and target quality. For uncomputed group g, measured action reward ultimately concerns gate-weighted W2 contribution, downstream norm/attention propagation and full free-running I2V, not simply ||W1_g x||². Separate the predictive correlation with hidden energy (easy label), native skip outcome at matched non-restoration budget (harder), real kernel acceleration and full-video quality (future authorized tests).

format_specific_scope.MXFP4: OCP E2M1 4-bit, local block32 E8M0 exponent-only scale. Effective s² can be represented as 2^(2e) for valid exponent; exponent bins are unusually compact amplitude features. The standard's conversion recipes may vary; encode only quantities actually stored in the selected runtime.
format_specific_scope.NVFP4: 16 elements/local FP8 E4M3 factor and FP32 global factor; some inference deployments use static/calibrated global scaling rather than per-token dynamic tensor amax. Weight side may use 2D 16x16 scaling; activation typically 1D 16. Inspect exact engine and its swizzled scale layout before promising cheap access.
format_specific_scope.HiF4_QDQ: Actual audited backend calculates 64-group lv0 scale, 8-subgroup lv1 and 4-subgroup lv2 internally, then writes dequantized values via native_hif4_activation_qdq as BF16 inputs to F.linear. Unless tapping existing quantizer intermediates in a newly engineered fused kernel, the metadata is NOT retained or directly addressable; recomputing max and scales is extra work. This backend is a scientific baseline, not the default platform for claimed metadata free-lunch.
format_specific_scope.other: Abstraction: encoder E(x)=(codes,side_state), side_state available at decision time with audited physical access cost; no specific exponent encoding is required to define the proxy.

mechanism.implementation_and_information_timing: For raw model/source claims, audit where the first quantizer writes metadata, whether a fused MMA overwrites/swizzles it, whether token grouping can be chosen before the main W1 kernel launch, and whether the router forces a synchronization. In QDQ, no exposed scale tensor means T0 is NOT a no-cost feature even if scale is computed inside a quant kernel. Comparisons should use native SAME-format dense reference and record extra kernels, packing and tensor-core utilization.
mechanism.analytic_counterexample: For an input block with amax=1 and effective scale fixed to 1, x_+=(1,1) and x_−=(1,−1) have identical scale and coordinate energies, but for W1 row (1,1), preactivations are 2 and 0. With GELU the output differs strongly; no scale-only function can distinguish these two cases. Likewise x=(6,0,...) and x'=(6,6,...) share amax/scale but have different code energy. Therefore P_scale is only a conditional/statistical proxy and requires signed-code/correlation competitors.
mechanism.strongest_competitors: Static offline W1/W2 block energy/sensitivity, original low-cost Q1 RMS already in earlier FFNDS group selection, group code-balance or scalar input norm, cheap learned router, and generic activation-aware quantization/outlier statistics (AWQ/Agile-Quant) for priority interpretation. Show added value over these before claiming a new algorithm.

competing_explanations: FFN group importance is determined by code SIGN and orientation rather than scale; same scale states induce opposite or cancelling W1 activations, so the scale-Gram score has no useful conditional ranking gain over static group weights.

Scale metadata is available physically in native FP4 but only after an expensive fused quantization or in a swizzled tensor, and exposing it needs a new launch or global-memory round trip that erases saved time.
Low-rank K factorization gives cheap ranks but discards highly anisotropic weight/activation covariance; learned code sketches are only as expensive as the original lightweight RMS proxy.
Strong W1 energy correlation does not predict GELU hidden selection or gate/W2/downstream video importance; a net-cost-aware value metric might reverse rankings.

Q1 on the actual A100 HiF4 path is QDQ→BF16 dense GEMM. Native MXFP4/NVFP4 may offer metadata cheaply on supported hardware but require separate implementation, format-matched dense baseline and may have different quantization distortions.
falsifiable_predictions: With an encoded native FP4 input, T0 per-microblock scale features are observable before W1 but will fail to distinguish equal-amax sign/opposition controls; T1 code-sign features may separate them at extra decoding cost.

Under isotropic block-code null, P_scale rank predicts group W1 preactivation squared norm better than fixed weight-only group norm when block scales vary; conditional dependence or anisotropy can falsify this.
For small rank r, K=UVᵀ can approximate coarse group-energy ranks with O(r(B+G)) arithmetic, but if actual native group-relevance differences live in small singular directions ranking may collapse.

Q2 metadata, if exposed, may improve post-W1 W2 decision but cannot improve pre-W1 action without a causal predictor or previous-state carryover; identical Q2 scale does not certify actual group output equality.

A usable native FP4 proxy must preserve net speed/quality at a held-out source cohort beyond fixed static group selection, a scalar block-RMS baseline and optimized FP4 dense reference, with scale access/packing charged.
best_counterexample: Two Q1 FP4-encoded inputs with x=(1,1) and x'=(1,−1) have identical block shared scale, max, squared energy and weight profile, but W1 row (1,1) sees z=2 versus z'=0. Thus any metadata-only method based on scale and unsigned block energy must rank them equally even though their GELU contributions differ; a code-direction feature is the specific missing information. For QDQ the supposed cheap input s may not even exist as a persistent tensor.
discussion_questions: Would the most useful observable be effective Q1 scale s, scale exponent e, per-block code occupancy, or the increment versus a previous token? How much relative value does each have after conditioning on ordinary Q1 RMS?
Can W1 output-group ranking be predicted by a rank-r quantizer metadata-Gram map without reading any packed data codes? If not, which ONE nibble statistic supplies the missing orientation?

Which Q1 scale metadata is physically available before W1 dispatch on selected native MXFP4/NVFP4 inference engines (and for current HiF4 QDQ)? Pin exact producer, memory layout and time/cost; do not use the training recipe as a stand-in for inference.

Can a proxy be sufficiently accurate for W1 + W2 group removal even if activation-energy labels are weak predictors of video quality? Which archived downstream evidence gives a no-regret or action-margin target?
Compare against existing Proxy+HWG/RMS selectors and static group choices: is there a causal signal genuinely added by quantization metadata rather than reusing already-known activation magnitude?
